subhead: You don’t need a gym or a free hour. Short bursts of movement add up, and they fit into a real workday.

article.title: Why short bursts count
paragraphs: U.S. physical activity guidelines recommend at least 150 minutes of moderate activity a week, about 22 minutes a day, plus muscle-strengthening activity two days a week. The good news: it doesn’t have to happen all at once.
The current guidelines dropped the old rule that activity had to come in 10-minute blocks to count. A brisk walk to the mailbox, a few flights of stairs, or a quick set of squats all add up.
Short movement breaks also interrupt the long stretches of sitting that come with many jobs. Getting up once an hour can ease stiffness and give your energy a lift.
article.closing: Pick one movement snack and attach it to something you already do every day. Once it sticks, add another.

quote.text: Some physical activity is better than none.

sideCard.title: Try a movement snack
sideCard.subtitle: Pick one. Pair it with something you already do.

sideCard.note: Talk with your doctor before starting a new exercise routine.

recipe.name: Three Sisters Stew
recipe.description: A hearty one-pot stew of beans, corn, and squash that’s even better the next day.
ingredients: ½ can low-sodium kidney beans, drained
steps: Brown the beef and onions in a skillet over medium-high heat for 8 to 10 minutes, until the beef reaches 160°F. Drain the fat.
In a large pot, combine the beef, water, and potatoes. Bring to a boil and cook for 15 minutes.
Add all of the remaining ingredients and return the pot to a boil.
Lower the heat and simmer for about 25 minutes.
Serve hot. Leftovers make an easy lunch the next day.
recipe.note: Why “Three Sisters”? Corn, beans, and squash have been grown together for generations, each helping the others thrive.

swaps.text: skip the beef and add the rest of both cans of beans.
low-sodium canned potatoes or carrots work too.
refrigerate within 2 hours; eat within 3 to 4 days.
